requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The repetitive procedure of taking a complete snapshot and re-evaluating all alternatives IS only a conceptual means for describing the semantics of the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The repetitive procedure of taking a complete snapshot and re-evaluate all alternatives is only a conceptual means for describing the semantics of the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The concrete algorithm that implements the `alt` statement semantics IS outside the scope of the TTCN-3 core language standard.
requirements.original: The concrete algorithm that implements this semantics is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: An alternative MAY be enabled or disabled by a Boolean expression placed between the "[" and "]" brackets of the alternative.
requirements.original: If necessary, it is possible to enable/disable an alternative by means of a Boolean expression placed between the ("[…]") brackets of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: Any branch in an `alt` statement MAY be defined as an else-branch by including the `else` keyword between the opening and closing brackets at the beginning of the alternative.
requirements.original: Any branch in an alt statement can be defined as an else branch by including the else keyword between the opening and closing brackets at the beginning of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no textually preceding alternative has proceeded
requirements.canonical: The statement block of an else-branch IS always executed if no other alternative textually preceding the else-branch has proceeded.
requirements.original: The statement block of the else branch is always executed if no other alternative textually preceding the else branch has proceeded.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: Unless the `@nodefault` modifier is present, the default mechanism IS always invoked at the end of all alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: It should be noted that the default mechanism (see clause 20.5) is always invoked at the end of all alternatives unless the @nodefault modifier is present.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: If an else-branch is defined in an `alt` statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called, i.e. active defaults are never entered.
requirements.original: If an else branch is defined, the default mechanism will never be called, i.e. active defaults will never be entered.

readings: If an else-branch is defined in an alt statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called for that alt statement at all.
If an else-branch is reached in an alt statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called; alternatives preceding the else-branch still have priority.
ambiguity.issue: Since the else-branch is always taken when reached, both readings give the same observable effect; the first, literal reading is chosen. It is unclear whether an else-branch inside an invoked altstep also suppresses the defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY contain an else-branch.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: It is also possible to use else in altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An else-branch MAY contain a `repeat` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: It is allowed to use a repeat statement within an else branch.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement or an altstep MAY define more than one else-branch.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: It is allowed to define more than one else branch in an alt statement or in an altstep, however always only the first else branch is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: more than one else-branch is defined
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement or altstep contains more than one else-branch, only the first else-branch IS ever executed.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: It is allowed to define more than one else branch in an alt statement or in an altstep, however always only the first else branch is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: The re-evaluation of an `alt` statement CAN be specified by a `repeat` statement.
requirements.original: The re-evaluation of an alt statement can be specified by using a repeat statement (see clause 20.3).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the invocation of altsteps as alternatives in alt statements (see clause 16.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.condition: an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative and one of its alternatives is selected
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL also be executed.
requirements.original: When an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call shall also be executed.

readings: When an alternative of an explicitly invoked altstep is selected and executed, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL also be executed.
Whenever an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL be executed, regardless of whether an altstep alternative was selected.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence omits the condition stated in 20.2-s024; the first reading (consistent with 20.2-s024) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement when a branch of the `alt` statement or of an invoked default is selected and completely executed.
requirements.original: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the alt statement when one of the branches of the alt or invoked defaults is selected and completely executed, or a branch of an altstep used in an altsteps-branch is selected and the branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement when a branch of an altstep used in an altstep-branch is selected and both that branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.
requirements.original: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the alt statement when one of the branches of the alt or invoked defaults is selected and completely executed, or a branch of an altstep used in an altsteps-branch is selected and the branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: a break statement is reached in the selected branch
requirements.canonical: Execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement if a `break` statement is reached in the statement block of the selected branch of the `alt` statement, of an altstep used in an altstep-branch, or of an altstep invoked as default.
requirements.original: Execution also continues with the statement following the alt statement if a break statement is reached in the statement block of the selected branch of an alt statement, of an altstep used in an altstep-branch, or of an `altstep` invoked as default.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement MAY be left by a `goto` statement in the selected branch of the `alt` statement, and execution continues with the statement following the label the `goto` points to.
requirements.original: The alt statement can also be left by using a goto statement in the selected branch of the alt (i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case), and execution continues with the statement following the label, `goto` is pointing to.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement CANNOT be used to leave an `alt` statement from a branch of an altstep or default.
requirements.original: The alt statement can also be left by using a goto statement in the selected branch of the alt (i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case), and execution continues with the statement following the label, `goto` is pointing to.

readings: A `goto` statement in a branch of an altstep or default SHALL NOT be used to leave the alt statement.
When an alt statement is left with `goto`, no altstep or default branches are evaluated (they are bypassed) since the goto is in a branch of the alt itself.
ambiguity.issue: The parenthesis "(i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case)" can be read as a restriction or as a consequence; the restriction reading is chosen, consistent with goto restrictions in 19.6.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The open and close square brackets "[" "]" SHALL be present at the start of each alternative of an `alt` statement, even if they are empty.
requirements.original: a) The open and close square brackets ("[…]") shall be present at the start of each alternative, even if they are empty.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The mandatory square brackets at the start of each alternative ARE necessary to syntactically distinguish one alternative from another and aid readability.
requirements.original: This not only aids readability but also is necessary to syntactically distinguish one alternative from another.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean expression guarding an alternative SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: b) The evaluation of a Boolean expression guarding an alternative shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard expression SHALL obey the same restrictions as the initialization of local definitions within altsteps and the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, the same restrictions as the restrictions for the initialization of local definitions within altsteps (clause 16.1.5) and the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of the event of an alt branch SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: c) The evaluation of the event of an alt branch shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression occurring in the matching part of an alternative SHALL obey the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component or introduce indeterminism in the evaluation of the following alt branches or the re-evaluation of the same alt branch, the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply to expressions occurring in the matching part of an alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.condition: none of the alternatives in the altstep is chosen
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternatives of an altstep invoked from an alt branch is chosen, the evaluation of that altstep SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: d) The evaluation of an altstep invoked from an alt branch, if none of the alternatives in the altstep is chosen, shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter of an altstep invoked from an alt branch SHALL obey the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply to the actual parameters of the invoked altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: the alt statement is used inside control behaviour
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement used inside control behaviour SHALL only contain timeout statements as alternatives.
requirements.original: f) An alt statement used inside control behaviour shall only contain timeout statements.

readings: An alt statement in control behaviour SHALL have only timeout-branches (and possibly else-branches).
An alt statement in control behaviour SHALL have only timeout-branches; else-branches and altstep-branches are also forbidden.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether else-branches (and altstep-branches whose altsteps only contain timeouts) are permitted; the first reading is chosen. "timeout statements" refers to timeout operations.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement IS used for a re-evaluation of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The repeat statement is used for a re-evaluation of an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement has the syntax `repeat`.
requirements.original: repeat

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in a statement block of an alt alternative
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in the statement block of an alternative of an `alt` statement causes the re-evaluation of the `alt` statement, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the alternatives are evaluated in the order of their specification.
requirements.original: The repeat statement, when used in the statement block of alternatives of alt statements, causes the re-evaluation of the alt statement, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the alternatives of the alt statement are evaluated in the order of their specification.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in the response and exception handling part of a blocking call
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in a statement block of the response and exception handling part of a blocking procedure call causes the re-evaluation of the response and exception handling part of the call.
requirements.original: When used in statement blocks of the response and exception handling parts of blocking procedure calls, the repeat statement causes the re-evaluation of the response and exception handling part of the call (see clause 22.3.1).

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in a top alternative of an altstep
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in a top alternative of an altstep definition causes a new snapshot and the re-evaluation of the `alt` statement from which the altstep has been called.
requirements.original: If a repeat statement is used in a top alternative in an altstep definition, it causes a new snapshot and the re-evaluation of the alt statement from which the altstep has been called.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep containing a `repeat` statement MAY be called either implicitly by the default mechanism or explicitly in an `alt` statement, with the same re-evaluation effect.
requirements.original: The call of the altstep may either be done implicitly by the default mechanism (see clause 20.5.1) or explicitly in the alt statement (see clause 20.2).

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement SHALL only be used within `alt` statements, `call` statements or altsteps.
requirements.original: a) The repeat statement shall only be used within alt statements, call statements or altsteps.

improper_terms.proper: response and exception handling part of a blocking call operation

ambiguity.issue: "call statements" is not a defined term; 20.3-s004 restricts the use to the response and exception handling part of blocking procedure calls.

non_requirement.reason: Paragraph heading "Invocation of altsteps as alternatives"
Paragraph heading "Continue execution after the alt statement"
Introductory sentence for the restrictions list; general rules are in clause 5 / table 16
